newsitem.title: UK: Clarke says stg was key factor in rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says stg was key factor in rate decision.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said the strength of sterling had been a key factor in his decision to leave interest rates unchanged after yesterday's monetary meeting.
"I set policy to keep inflation down," he told Sky Television.

"The key thing that influenced me was -- not the only thing that influenced me -- the strength of sterling. We've seen sterling go up rapidly in value. That cuts down our costs but it reduces the value of our export sales. That's deflationary."
Clarke said that at each monthly monetary meeting, he looked at all relevant factors in setting policy.

"I decided to make no change yesterday. Every time I look at the overall picture, I'll keep asking myself "what do we need to do to keep inflation down? What do we need to do to keep the conditions in place for UK Ltd to carry on doing so well?'"
Clarke said the housing market was strong, the labour market was in good condition and consumer demand was strong.
"But the retailers said it wasn't a boom at Christmas, just a good Christmas -- sounds quite reassuring. Manufacturing production is still a bit flat."
In an earlier interview with ITN, Clarke said the Conservative government would stick to a tax-cutting agenda whenever it could.
"I believe in introducing budgets to cut tax once I've got the recovery underway and borrowing under control," he said.
